summary:
"Product of everything except index i" = (product of everything **left** of i) × (product of everything
**right** of i). Both are running products: one pass from the left, one from the right. Storing the left
products in the answer array itself and carrying the right product in a variable gives O(n) time and
O(1) extra space, with no division.

question.md:
For every index i, return the product of all elements **except** `nums[i]`, without using division.

- **Why no division?** The obvious trick, "total product ÷ nums[i]", breaks on zeros: with one zero,
  every other answer is 0 but the zero's own answer isn't; with two zeros, all answers are 0. The
  no-division rule forces an approach that handles zeros naturally.
- **Values are −2 … 2**, and at most 60 of them are ±2, so every answer fits in a 64-bit integer
  (|answer| ≤ 2⁶⁰). Use `long` in Java and C++/C.
- **Size:** up to 10⁵, so the O(n²) "multiply all the others" is too slow.

think.md:
Take `[3, −1, 2, 2, −2]`. For index 2, the answer is `3 × (−1)` (left of it) times `2 × (−2)` (right of
it) = −3 × −4 = 12.

think.caption: Everything except index 2 = the left block × the right block.

think.md:
Every answer splits the same way: left block × right block. And the left blocks grow one element at a
time as i moves right (`1`, `3`, `3 × −1`, …), so all of them come from **one running product**. The
same is true of the right blocks from the other end. Two passes, no division, and zeros need no special
handling: a zero simply makes every block that contains it 0.

approaches.title: Multiply all the others for each index

idea.md: For each i, loop over every j ≠ i and multiply. Direct, but each answer redoes almost the same work.

build: For each i: start a product at 1.

lines.text: Multiply every element except the one at i. 64-bit, since products reach 2⁶⁰.

walk.title: For each index, multiply every other element.

limits.md: The products for i and i + 1 share all but two factors, yet each is rebuilt from scratch. Running products from both ends share that work.

idea.md: Build `prefix[i]` = product of `nums[0 … i − 1]` (with `prefix[0] = 1`) and `suffix[i]` = product of `nums[i + 1 … n − 1]` (with `suffix[n − 1] = 1`). Then `answer[i] = prefix[i] × suffix[i]`.

lines.text: Product of everything strictly left of i. Index 0 has nothing on its left, so its product is the empty product, 1.
Product of everything strictly right of i, built from the end the same way.
Left part × right part = everything except i.

notes.c: Free the two helper arrays; the caller frees `out`.

complexity.md: **Time O(n):** three passes. **Space O(n)** for the two helper arrays.

steps.text: prefix[0] = 1 (nothing on the left); each next one multiplies in one more element.
suffix[n − 1] = 1 (nothing on the right); built the same way from the right.

walk.title: prefix[i] = product of everything left of i; suffix[i] = product of everything right of i. The answer is their product.

limits.md: Two extra arrays of size n. The output array can hold the prefix products, and the suffix product only needs to exist one index at a time.

approaches.title: Left products in the output, right product on the fly

idea.md: Pass 1 (left to right): write the running left product into `out[i]` *before* multiplying in `nums[i]`. Pass 2 (right to left): keep `right`, the product of everything after i, multiply it into `out[i]`, then multiply `nums[i]` into `right`.

build: `left = 1`; for i from 0: `out[i] = left`, then `left *= nums[i]`.
`right = 1`; for i from n − 1 down: `out[i] *= right`, then `right *= nums[i]`.

lines.text: The answer array doubles as storage for the left products.
Write the product of everything **before** i, then include `nums[i]` for the next index. The order of these two lines is what excludes `nums[i]` itself.
Same idea from the right: multiply in the product of everything **after** i, then include `nums[i]`.

complexity.md: **Time O(n):** two passes. **Space O(1)** besides the output.

steps.text: Left pass: out[i] = product of everything before i.
Right pass at 4: multiply by right = 1 (product of everything after 4) → -12.
Right pass at 3: multiply by right = -2 (product of everything after 3) → 12.
Right pass at 2: multiply by right = -4 (product of everything after 2) → 12.
Right pass at 1: multiply by right = -8 (product of everything after 1) → -24.
Right pass at 0: multiply by right = 8 (product of everything after 0) → 8.

walk.title: Store the left products in the answer array, then sweep from the right with a running product.

takeaways.md:
- "All except i" = **prefix up to i − 1** combined with **suffix from i + 1**. Works for products, sums,
  maxima, …
- Write the running value *before* folding in the current element to exclude it.
- The output array can store one direction's results; carry the other direction in a variable.
